import argparse
import pyaes

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--key', type=str, required=True)  # 16 bytes key
    parser.add_argument('--iv', type=str, required=True)   # 16 bytes IV
    parser.add_argument('--data1', type=str, required=True) # 16 bytes data
    parser.add_argument('--data2', type=str, required=True) # 16 bytes data
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    # Create AES CBC cipher
    aes = pyaes.AESModeOfOperationCBC(args.key.encode(), args.iv.encode())  # Initialize AES CBC cipher
    # Encrypt two data blocks
    ciphertext1 = aes.encrypt(args.data1.encode())  # Encrypt first plaintext
    ciphertext2 = aes.encrypt(args.data2.encode())  # Encrypt second plaintext
    print(ciphertext1)
    print(ciphertext2)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

item.text: The implementation is functionally done. I’m running one normalized parity sweep against the executable now, so I can catch any last mismatches across both success and failure cases before I hand it over.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat <<'EOF' >/tmp/test7_parity.sh
normalize() {
  sed -E \"s/test7_executable/test7.mjs/g; s/\\[PYI-[0-9]+:/[PYI-PID:/g\"
}

run_case() {
  name=\""'$1"
  shift

  node /output/test7.mjs "$@" >/tmp/node.out 2>/tmp/node.err
  node_rc=$?
  /workspace/dataset/test7_executable "$@" >/tmp/exe.out 2>/tmp/exe.err
  exe_rc=$?

  normalize </tmp/node.out >/tmp/node.out.norm
  normalize </tmp/node.err >/tmp/node.err.norm
  normalize </tmp/exe.out >/tmp/exe.out.norm
  normalize </tmp/exe.err >/tmp/exe.err.norm

  if [ "$node_rc" -ne "$exe_rc" ]; then
    echo "$name: rc mismatch node=$node_rc exe=$exe_rc"
    return
  fi

  if ! cmp -s /tmp/node.out.norm /tmp/exe.out.norm; then
    echo "$name: stdout mismatch"
    return
  fi

  if ! cmp -s /tmp/node.err.norm /tmp/exe.err.norm; then
    echo "$name: stderr mismatch"
    return
  fi

  echo "$name: OK"
}
